title: Lalremsiami's strike, Bichu Devi's wall of resistance power India to hockey gold, LA Olympics berth
subtitle: Lalremsiami's superb reverse-stick strike in the 10th minute gave India the lead, but it was goalkeeper Bichu Devi's heroics and a defence that refused to yield that ultimately settled the final.
summary: A masterclass in tactical discipline and heroic goalkeeping as the Indian women's hockey team captures Asian Games gold and punches its official ticket to the Los Angeles Olympic Games.
content: In one of the most thrilling hockey finals in recent memory, India's women's hockey squad defended their hearts out to secure a memorable 1-0 victory, claiming Asian Games gold and an automatic berth for the upcoming Los Angeles Olympic Games.

The defining offensive moment arrived in the 10th minute when forward Lalremsiami, receiving a pinpoint cross from the right flank, controlled the ball on the spin and fired an unstoppable reverse-stick drive into the top left corner.

From that moment on, it was an exhibition of sheer defensive grit. In the fourth quarter alone, India conceded four penalty corners under intense offensive bombardment. Each time, goalkeeper Bichu Devi stood tall, producing reflex stick saves and clearing rebounds under suffocating pressure.

“We promised each other that not a single inch would be given easily,” Lalremsiami remarked after the final whistle. “Every drop of sweat in the training camps over the last three years was for this flag and this gold medal.”
With this victory, the squad secures direct qualification for LA 2028, cementing their position among the world's elite hockey nations.

title: I wanted to quit boxing but I continued, had to change colour of Asiad medal: Lovlina
summary: Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain opens up about self-doubt, rigorous tactical transformations, and her relentless drive to upgrade her Asian Games medal into gold.
content: In an emotional and candid interview following her podium triumph, Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain revealed that she had seriously contemplated stepping away from competitive boxing during the peak of training exhaustion.

“There were days when the physical toll and the tactical adjustments felt overwhelming. But I made a quiet vow to myself: I had to change the colour of the medal. I couldn't stop at bronze when India was counting on me,” she said.

Lovlina reworked her footwork and infighting defence over ten grueling months in Patiala, focusing on counter-punching against taller southpaws. Her perseverance bore fruit with a dominating performance that secured her berth at the upcoming Olympic qualifiers.

title: Four Indian brands putting a new spin on khadi
summary: From high-fashion jackets in Milan to everyday urban streetwear, how indigenous artisan collectives and modern designers are redefining India's heritage fabric.
content: Khadi is no longer confined to traditional national occasions. A rising wave of contemporary homegrown brands is fusing handspun, zero-carbon cotton and silk with modern cuts, neutral tones, and durable tailoring.

By collaborating directly with weaver clusters across West Bengal, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh, these labels ensure living wages for rural artisans while introducing khadi to Gen Z and millennial wardrobes.

“We want people to touch the fabric and realise that it is the ultimate natural luxury: breathable in heat, insulated in cool evenings, and entirely biodegradable,” says one of the featured designers.

title: Telangana, Maharashtra, UP lead state rankings in data centre policy attractiveness: S&P Global
summary: A comprehensive S&P Global ratings report highlights state-level power tariffs, renewable energy zoning, and single-window statutory clearances as key drivers of hyperscale cloud capacity.
content: India's data centre capacity is projected to cross 2.5 Gigawatts by 2027, driven by exponential generative AI training and strict local data residency mandates.

According to S&P Global, Telangana, Maharashtra, and Uttar Pradesh have outpaced neighboring industrial corridors by offering subsidized dual-grid electricity, fast-track environmental clearance, and dedicated sub-sea cable landing connectivity in coastal regions.
Global hyperscalers including AWS, Microsoft, and Google have committed multi-billion dollar capital expenditure plans in Hyderabad and Navi Mumbai over the next five fiscal years.

title: White-collar hiring grows 2% led by AI/ML sector in Sep: Report
summary: Specialized roles in machine learning deployment, computer vision, and neural network optimization saw a 28% year-on-year surge, stabilizing broad white-collar recruitment indices.
content: While traditional IT recruitment and generalist software engineering remained flat, hiring for artificial intelligence, machine learning ops (MLOps), and specialized data architecture recorded brisk sequential momentum.

The latest monthly employment tracker reveals that Bengaluru and Hyderabad accounted for over 48% of all high-value tech openings, with salary premiums for senior AI researchers expanding significantly.
“Companies are no longer doing speculative mass hiring. Every open requisition requires demonstrated capability in deploying large-scale automated pipelines,” said a leading HR executive.

title: India's IT services pyramid Is hollowing out from the middle
summary: As AI code generation automates mid-tier software testing and legacy maintenance, India's $250 billion IT giants face a structural squeeze on mid-level managerial pyramids.
content: For three decades, the Indian IT services delivery model operated on a predictable pyramidal hierarchy: thousands of fresh campus recruits at the base, project leads and middle managers in the center, and client partners at the apex.

Now, enterprise customers are demanding outcome-based billing rather than billable man-hours. Generative AI agents are completing in minutes tasks that previously required a team of four mid-level analysts.

This structural shift is compelling Indian tech giants to retrain hundreds of thousands of staff into specialized solutions architects, prompting the steepest reshaping of white-collar IT careers in a generation.

title: If AI is writing your resume, then what?
summary: When both applicants and hiring managers rely on automated LLM agents, recruitment devolves into a game of algorithmic cat-and-mouse. How companies are returning to real-world proof-of-work.
content: Candidate resumes have become uniformly flawless: keyword-optimized, grammatically immaculate, and crafted by generative AI. On the receiving end, corporate ATS algorithms parse and filter thousands of synthetic profiles per hour.

The result is reciprocal exhaustion. Top tier startups and engineering teams are quietly discarding standard resumes in favor of live code walkthroughs, verifiable GitHub repositories, and paid trial projects.
“We don't care how eloquently your CV is written,” says a seed fund founder. “Show us what you built under production pressure last month.”

title: Under Ronnie Screwvala’s watch, upGrad is chasing PhysicsWallah, Eruditus
summary: Navigating post-pandemic market consolidation, upGrad bets heavily on university-accredited higher degrees and hybrid offline coaching centers to challenge valuation peers.
content: The Indian education technology landscape has shifted dramatically from hyper-funded customer acquisition into ruthless unit economic discipline.
Under Ronnie Screwvala's leadership, upGrad has pivoted away from short unaccredited micro-courses towards multi-year degrees in partnership with top global institutions.
With offline exam prep centers and corporate enterprise training contracts stabilizing cash flows, the company is preparing for an eventual domestic public listing.

title: India’s top AI teams set to battle in Elastic and AWS's Forge the Future Hackathon finale
subtitle: After weeks of registration, idea submission, and shortlisting, finalists compete in Bengaluru with the winners earning a place at Elastic{ON} Mumbai.
summary: Top AI teams compete in Bengaluru for a grand prize and showcase at Elastic{ON} Mumbai.
content: The Grand Finale of the Elastic and AWS 'Forge the Future' Hackathon in Bengaluru brings together India's finest machine learning engineers.
Finalist teams demonstrated production-grade agentic search workflows, multi-modal database retrieval, and enterprise compliance tools.
The competition highlights India's swift transition from generic API wrappers into robust deep tech architectures.

title: EquityList launches AI-native cap table and compliance OS
subtitle: The company, which manages more than $20 billion in securities across 650+ companies and 80,000+ stakeholders, introduces agentic AI capabilities.
summary: EquityList introduces agentic AI to interpret legal term sheets and automate statutory filings.
content: EquityList has unveiled a major technology upgrade designed to eliminate human friction from ESOP administration and cap table compliance.
The system automatically interprets term sheets, calculates dilution cascades, and generates statutory filings in seconds.
With 80,000+ stakeholders on the platform, founders can now offer liquid secondary tender offers with zero administrative overhead.

title: How new broadcast technology is changing the way fans watch cricket
subtitle: Immersive multi-angle cameras, AI-led graphics, and fan-powered sight screens redefine live sports entertainment.
summary: Spatial cameras and neural networks deliver real-time predictive analytics to cricket streaming fans.
content: Modern cricket broadcasting has evolved into a high-bandwidth spatial computing experience.
New computer vision algorithms analyze ball spin RPM, trajectory deviations, and fielding reaction times in milliseconds.
Viewers can select personalized player cameras and interactive replay angles directly from their mobile apps.

title: Why Rubrik believes cyber resilience, not prevention, is the next frontier
subtitle: As AI compresses cyberattacks from weeks to seconds, enterprises must prepare to recover from breaches, not just prevent them.
summary: Why perimeter security is obsolete, making immutable zero-trust backups the true benchmark.
content: In modern enterprise security, the premise of an impregnable network perimeter is obsolete.
Rubrik's immutable data architecture ensures that even in the catastrophic event of a full active directory compromise, uncorrupted backup snapshots can restore critical operations.
Boardrooms are recognizing that resilience—the ability to resume operations within hours rather than paying ransoms—is the true benchmark of security.

title: Meet Nuvr, the bootstrapped startup managing Rs 1,200 Cr of ecommerce sales for brands
subtitle: The Bengaluru-based startup runs online P&Ls for brands such as Medimix, Nilon’s, and Origami, using its own technology and a performance-linked revenue model.
summary: The bootstrapped startup scales digital P&Ls and ecommerce fulfillment across leading consumer brands.
content: Nuvr is proving that capital efficiency and operational rigor trump venture-fueled burn.
The startup manages the complete digital P&L for FMCG leaders including Medimix, Nilon's, and Origami, ensuring profitability across Amazon, Flipkart, and quick-commerce channels.
Their proprietary inventory forecasting software prevents costly stockouts and slashes marketplace deductions.

title: Silence Laboratories is building privacy-first cybersecurity technology
subtitle: Operating out of Palo Alto and Bengaluru, the startup works with around 35 clients globally, including top US financial institutions.
summary: Decentralized multi-party computation secures institutional crypto and fintech assets globally.
content: Silence Laboratories eliminates single points of failure in private key custody.
By mathematically splitting authorization across independent nodes, transactions are signed without any single server reconstructing the full secret.
The team works with leading fintechs and global commercial banks across North America and Asia.

title: Quantum World Ventures looks to move the technology beyond the lab
subtitle: The Bengaluru-based startup is developing quantum and AI applications for medical technology while exploring security applications.
summary: Pioneering real-world quantum algorithms for early molecular simulation and healthcare diagnostics.
content: Quantum computing is transitioning from academic whiteboards into practical enterprise testbeds.
Quantum World Ventures is building quantum algorithms for early molecular simulation and healthcare diagnostics.
The founders are pioneering quantum education programs to train the next generation of Indian hardware and algorithmic physicists.

title: Freshworks Co-Founder Girish Mathrubootham turns film producer for Tamil sports drama 'Sarpatta Parambarai 2'
summary: Freshworks co-founder and SaaS pioneer Girish Mathrubootham ventures into film financing as co-producer for Pa Ranjith's highly anticipated period boxing drama sequel.
content: In an unexpected crossover between technology entrepreneurship and Indian regional cinema, Freshworks co-founder Girish Mathrubootham has officially boarded 'Sarpatta Parambarai 2' as co-producer.
The sequel to director Pa Ranjith's critically acclaimed 2021 boxing drama is slated to go on floors later this year, with actor Arya reprising his lead role as Kabilan.
Mathrubootham remarked that supporting regional storytelling with authentic local grit has always been a passion outside of scaling global software enterprises from Chennai.

title: Restrictions on social media for under-18? SC asks Centre to examine statutory safeguards for minors
summary: The Supreme Court directs Union ministries to formulate institutional guidelines preventing algorithmic addiction and behavioral harm among adolescents.
content: The Supreme Court of India has instructed the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to examine statutory age verifications and screen-time restrictions for users under 18.
The bench underscored rising neurological and mental health concerns stemming from dark pattern algorithms and infinite scrolling feeds on major video-sharing platforms.
Tech industry representatives have urged consultative frameworks that balance child protection with access to legitimate educational internet resources.

title: CoinSwitch turns profitable in FY26 on adjusted EBITDA as revenue jumps 150%
summary: Crypto exchange platform CoinSwitch posts positive operating cash flow and a 150% surge in annualized gross turnover following diversification into mutual funds and fixed deposits.
content: India's largest crypto asset aggregator CoinSwitch has reported operational profitability on an adjusted EBITDA basis for fiscal year 2026.

Co-founders Ashish Singhal, Govind Soni, and Vimal Sagar Tiwari highlighted that disciplined overhead rationalization coupled with multi-asset expansion into equities and sovereign bonds drove the turnaround.
The platform now boasts over 20 million registered users, with non-crypto retail wealth products accounting for nearly 30% of monthly platform activity.

title: IIM Kozhikode partners with Walmart Global Tech to nurture Indian deeptech startups
summary: A premier academic incubator and global retail tech giant roll out equity-free innovation grants and executive mentorship for AI and supply chain pioneers.
content: The Indian Institute of Management Kozhikode (IIMK) through its Laboratory for Innovation, Venturing and Entrepreneurship (LIVE) has inked an alliance with Walmart Global Tech.
The multi-year acceleration cohort will provide equity-free grant financing, compute credits, and direct enterprise pilots for early-stage B2B supply chain innovators.
Selected startups will work alongside Walmart's Bengaluru engineering teams to stress-test automated inventory intelligence and edge predictive algorithms.

title: Bharat Housing Network secures $5M from Symbiotics
summary: Affordable housing infrastructure enabler Bharat Housing Network raises fresh external debt to disburse small-ticket loans across tier-3 and tier-4 regions.
content: Bharat Housing Network has secured $5 million in structured credit financing from Swiss impact asset manager Symbiotics Investments.
The platform coordinates capital between mainstream institutional financiers and localized housing finance companies serving informal-income borrowers.
The funds will bolster mortgage penetration for self-employed micro-entrepreneurs in semi-urban India constructing first-time residential dwellings.

title: India faces 53-60% talent gap in GenAI, cloud skills: TeamLease
summary: Industry staffing benchmark reports widening deficit between enterprise demand for LLM orchestration engineers and domestic engineering graduates.
content: A comprehensive talent survey by TeamLease Digital indicates that Indian IT services and enterprise GCCs are grappling with a 53% to 60% shortage of qualified GenAI engineers.
While over 1.5 million engineering students graduate annually, fewer than 8% possess hands-on familiarity with transformer architectures, vector embeddings, and RAG pipelines.
Corporate training academies are accelerating internal upskilling programs to prevent wage inflation and fill over 80,000 vacant specialist roles.

title: Adani Family Office backs Nudge as startup pivots to rewards-led credit ecosystem
summary: Meet Shah's consumer fintech venture secures strategic capital to build a seamless lifestyle loyalty reward program for next-gen cardholders.
content: In a notable institutional vote of confidence, the Adani Family Office has invested in consumer rewards startup Nudge as part of its pre-Series A syndicate.
Founder Meet Shah stated that the platform is revamping loyalty economics by allowing consumers to consolidate disparate merchant points into real-time portfolio credits.
The capital injection will finance co-branded credit card rollouts with leading private sector banks across Mumbai, Delhi NCR, and Bengaluru.

title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (September 29, 2026)
summary: Your daily recap of early-stage funding rounds, leadership reshuffles, policy updates, and executive appointments shaping India's venture landscape.
content: The Indian startup ecosystem recorded 11 funding deals totaling $42 million today, headlined by seed-stage deeptech and fintech debt rounds.
Meanwhile, SEBI issued consultative clarifications regarding employee stock ownership plans (ESOPs) and secondary liquidity windows for pre-IPO unicorns.
Leading venture partners expressed optimism regarding late-stage valuation stabilization as domestic institutional inflows hit quarterly highs.

title: Women entrepreneurs lead record 28% of early-stage venture rounds in tier-2 India
summary: Female-founded enterprises across Jaipur, Kochi, and Chandigarh command accelerated angel checks in D2C healthcare and climate tech.
content: Indian female founders are capturing an unprecedented share of early-stage institutional venture financing across tier-2 urban corridors.
According to recent market data, over 28% of institutional seed syndicates closed this quarter featured solo women founders or female co-founders.
Venture partners attribute the expansion to specialized mentorship cohorts and tailored angel networks fostering grassroots innovation.

title: Ola Electric approves Rs 1,500 Cr rights issue to fund Gigafactory expansion
summary: Bhavish Aggarwal backs Ola Electric's Rs 1,500 crore capital enhancement plan by committing personal equity pledges to anchor domestic expansion.
content: Ola Electric founder and chief executive Bhavish Aggarwal has led board approval for a Rs 1,500 crore rights issue to accelerate cell manufacturing at its Tamil Nadu Gigafactory.
The expansion aims to scale domestic 4680 lithium-ion cell production and cut reliance on battery imports ahead of volume vehicle deliveries.
Market analysts note the rights issue provides vital working capital cushion as electric two-wheeler market penetration crosses 8% nationally.

title: Agnikul Cosmos prepares sub-orbital rocket mission following launchpad validation
summary: The Chennai spacetech pioneer achieves 100% mission burn duration on its 3D-printed rocket propulsion stages.
content: Spacetech pioneer Agnikul Cosmos has cleared long-duration hot-fire testing for its semi-cryogenic rocket upper stage.
Engineered through industrial additive manufacturing in a single print run, the engine performed within tight nominal pressure parameters across 180 seconds of full thrust.
The milestone clears the path for the startup's planned orbital launch missions for commercial micro-satellites.

title: Swiggy updates DRHP with fresh financials ahead of landmark public market debut
summary: Updated financials reveal robust contribution margins in food delivery and accelerated dark store density for quick commerce Instamart.
content: Consumer internet leader Swiggy submitted an updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus to SEBI, indicating significant profitability improvements across its core food delivery division.
Instamart recorded sharp quarterly volume growth, adding over 150 dark fulfillment stores in tier-1 metro clusters.
Institutional investors are keenly evaluating secondary sale components and anchor allocations for the impending multi-billion dollar public offering.

title: Zomato launches 'District' app for dining, movie tickets, and live event bookings
summary: Dedicated going-out super app combines restaurant table reservations, concert passes, and entertainment ticketing into a standalone consumer portal.
content: Food tech giant Zomato has officially debuted 'District', a specialized standalone application consolidating out-of-home leisure experiences.
The app bridges dining out reservations with live music events, comedy shows, and multiplex movie ticketing, directly competing with incumbent entertainment portals.
Founder Deepinder Goyal noted that out-of-home lifestyle experiences represent an underpenetrated multi-billion dollar opportunity across urban India.

title: Pine Labs secures RBI approval to operate as payment aggregator in India
summary: The merchant commerce titan strengthens online omnichannel checkout solutions under formal Reserve Bank regulatory oversight.
content: Pine Labs has received coveted in-principle authorization from the Reserve Bank of India to operate as a full-stack online payment aggregator.
The regulatory sanction validates the fintech veteran's compliance architecture, enabling direct merchant on-boarding for web and app payments.
Leadership highlighted plans to integrate conversational commerce checkouts and instant digital settlements for small retailers.

title: Peak XV Partners leads $25M Series A round in Fabless Semiconductor startup
summary: Semiconductor innovators build ultra-low-power neural processing units designed to run large language models on edge devices.
content: In one of the largest early-stage semiconductor rounds of the quarter, deeptech innovator NeuroEdge has closed an $18 million Series A syndicate.
The round was spearheaded by Peak XV Partners with participation from Lightspeed and prominent Silicon Valley angel syndicates.
Proceeds will finance tape-out cycles for custom sub-4nm processor architectures targeting industrial IoT and smart automotive cameras.

title: Zerodha Fund House surpasses Rs 5,000 Cr in AUM driven by passive index funds
summary: A joint venture between Zerodha and Smallcase achieves rapid retail asset growth purely through zero-commission, direct-to-consumer index products.
content: Zerodha Fund House has achieved Rs 5,000 crore in assets under management in just 14 months of launching operations.
The asset management firm focuses exclusively on rule-based, passive index mutual funds and ETFs with industry-low expense ratios.
Over 85% of investment inflows originated from tier-2 and tier-3 towns through mobile-first brokerage accounts.

title: Lenskart commissions mega manufacturing facility in Bhiwadi to expand output
summary: Robotic injection molding and precision German laser edging equipment double eyewear output to 50 million pairs annually.
content: Eyewear unicorn Lenskart has inaugurated its massive 500,000 sq ft smart manufacturing campus in Bhiwadi, Rajasthan.
Equipped with automated guided vehicles and automated prescription lens cutters, the plant drastically cuts turnaround times for international deliveries.
Founder Peyush Bansal stated that over 60% of output will serve exports across Southeast Asia and the Middle East.

title: Groww surpasses 12 million active clients, cementing lead in mutual fund distribution
summary: The discount brokerage hits 12 million active traders, commanding the highest market share on the National Stock Exchange.
content: Latest monthly data released by the National Stock Exchange shows fintech platform Groww consolidating its position as India's largest retail brokerage.
With active client counts surmounting 12 million, the platform attributed its market share lead to frictionless paperless KYC and zero account maintenance charges.
The company is currently preparing to expand into algorithmic trading tools and wealth management advisory services.

title: Flipkart deploys 25,000 electric delivery vehicles ahead of festive sale season
summary: Commercial EV fleet partnerships with Hero Electric and Euler Motors power zero-emission last-mile express deliveries across 200 cities.
content: In a major environmental sustainability push, Flipkart's hyperlocal fulfillment arm has deployed 25,000 commercial electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers.
The fleet integration cuts last-mile delivery carbon emissions by thousands of tons during peak festive shopping spikes.
Battery swapping stations installed across regional dark stores enable round-the-clock delivery availability without prolonged charging downtime.

title: Sarvam AI launches open-source Indic LLMs tailored for Indian enterprise workflows
summary: Bespoke language models natively benchmarked across 10 official Indian languages achieve parity with leading global closed-source models.
content: Deeptech generative AI startup Sarvam AI has publicly released its open weights foundation model trained on high-fidelity multilingual corpora.
Designed specifically for voice-first interactions and vernacular nuance, the model excels in legal summarization, banking bots, and public health advisories.
Enterprise clients in banking and telecommunications are already deploying the model within private cloud VPC environments.

title: KredX secures non-banking finance company licence from Reserve Bank of India
summary: Supply chain financier KredX gains direct balance-sheet lending capabilities to underwrite vendor invoices for tier-2 manufacturers.
content: Invoice discounting and enterprise working capital platform KredX has been granted a NBFC license from the Reserve Bank of India.
The certification permits the company to co-lend and underwrite customized cash flow credit directly to MSME suppliers.
CEO Manish Kumar emphasized that the regulatory milestone will unlock over Rs 2,500 crore in seasonal working capital for export vendors.

title: Urban Company turns cash flow positive with strong home repair salon demand
summary: Operational discipline, international salon expansion in UAE and Singapore, and Native water purifier sales push gig services leader into net cash generation.
content: On-demand home services major Urban Company has achieved sustained net cash flow positivity across consecutive financial quarters.
The turnaround was fueled by higher repeat customer frequency in urban salon treatments and margin expansion from its proprietary Native water purifier range.
The company continues to prepare for an eventual domestic public market listing with strong positive unit economics.

title: Ather Energy files updated draft prospectus for Rs 4,500 Cr IPO
summary: Electric scooter manufacturer Ather Energy plans primary share issuance to finance its new manufacturing hub in Maharashtra.
content: Bengaluru-based EV maker Ather Energy has filed updated documents with market regulator SEBI for its proposed initial public offering.
The issue will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 3,100 crore alongside an offer for sale from existing early institutional backers.
The fresh capital will back R&D for next-generation family electric scooters and expanding Ather Grid fast-charging locations.

title: Daily tech & venture wrap: Indian startups raise $180M across 14 deals
summary: Growth capital rebounds as enterprise AI, clean mobility, and private credit platforms close robust institutional funding rounds.
content: Venture deployment across Indian startups gathered momentum today with $180 million invested in growth and early stage ventures.
Venture debt and secondary deals also featured prominently as institutional allocators expressed confidence in domestic macroeconomic fundamentals.
Founders highlighted disciplined runway management and clear profitability roadmaps as key factors driving term sheet execution.

title: Andhra, Chhattisgarh, Bihar are outsmarting richer states on investments (without outspending)
subtitle: A licence, a statute and a purchase contract: how three challenger states are gaining ground without simply writing bigger subsidy cheques.
summary: How challenger states attract major industrial capital through regulatory speed and certainty.
content: For years, industrial capital in India flowed overwhelmingly towards established coastal hubs like Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Tamil Nadu.

However, a structural shift is taking place. Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Bihar are securing massive renewable and manufacturing commitments through statutory single-window approvals and plug-and-play industrial infrastructure.
“Capital seeks certainty and speed rather than temporary tax sops,” explains an infrastructure policy director.

title: Why India imports apples despite record production, and how to fix it
subtitle: Cold chain fragmentation, high post-harvest transit losses, and the agronomy bottlenecks holding back Himalayan orchardists.
summary: Solving cold chain transit losses to help domestic Himalayan apple orchards compete.
content: India produces over 2.5 million metric tons of apples each season, yet imported produce from Washington, Turkey, and New Zealand commands premium supermarket shelf space.
The culprit is inadequate controlled-atmosphere storage and road freight bruising during downhill transit.
A new generation of agri-logistics startups is introducing farm-gate sorting, dynamic precooling chambers, and cold chain telemetry to reverse this trade imbalance.

title: India has cracked rocket science. Now comes the hard part: Rocket Economics
subtitle: Agnikul CEO: “We Can’t Build Use-and-Throw Systems If We Want to Be a Business”
summary: Spacetech enters the commercial era where turnaround cadence and reusability dictate survival.
content: Proving that a single-piece 3D-printed rocket engine works in flight is a tremendous engineering milestone.
Now, the ruthless laws of commercial aviation are taking over. To generate sustainable returns for institutional investors, launch providers must achieve rapid turnarounds.
Agnikul's leadership discusses their semi-cryogenic propulsion economics, mobile pad architectures, and why reusability is existential for commercial spacetech.

title: The $2 Million Startup Building an Operating System for India's Apple Industry
subtitle: Agritech pioneers deploy spectral imaging and AI grading to modernize fruit sorting across Kashmir and Himachal orchards.
summary: Computer vision grading booths eliminate middlemen and boost orchard farm-gate margins.
content: Instead of subjective manual inspection where growers frequently suffer arbitrary grade discounts at wholesale mandis, new spectral imaging sensors measure sugar brix and internal firmness non-invasively.
Growers receive instant algorithmic quality certification and digital payments on their phones, unlocking fair prices from organized retail buyers.

title: His software is inside your router. Now he wants it inside much smaller things
subtitle: How Chennai deep tech firm embedUR Systems went from powering enterprise Wi-Fi to edge IoT and AI micro-controllers.
summary: Bootstrapped software pioneer scales from enterprise Wi-Fi routers into embedded edge AI chips.
content: Chances are high that the wireless router providing your internet connection runs firmware written by embedUR Systems.
Founder Rajesh C. built a global embedded software powerhouse from Chennai with zero venture capital, serving Tier-1 telecom providers.
Now, the company is compressing deep neural networks onto microscopic IoT silicon to enable smart home intelligence without round-trip cloud latency.

title: Trump calls for artificial intelligence to be renamed 'super intelligence' in the US
subtitle: Speaking at an international tech forum, the former president advocated elevating generative AI benchmarks into federal strategic dominance policy.
summary: During remarks addressing global semiconductor leadership and quantum compute, discussions centered around classifying foundational frontier models under sovereign defense frameworks.
content: In remarks delivered before tech industry executives, Donald Trump proposed rebranding standard artificial intelligence to 'super intelligence', arguing that contemporary multi-modal reasoning systems have surpassed historical machine learning definitions.
The speech underscored ongoing geopolitical debates regarding algorithmic sovereignty, export controls on high-bandwidth memory chips, and federal funding allocations for national compute clusters.
Venture analysts noted that while semantic branding may shift, enterprise focus remains laser-focused on model reliability, inference costs, and real-world deployment efficiency.

title: Sarvam AI launches open-source Indic LLMs tailored for Indian enterprise workflows
subtitle: Bespoke 2B and 7B parameter models trained natively on 10 official Indian languages achieve breakthrough accuracy in legal summarization and voice bots.
summary: Deeptech pioneer Sarvam AI releases open weights models optimized for cost-effective local inference on enterprise CPU and consumer GPU clusters.
content: Bengaluru-based deep tech venture Sarvam AI has publicly released its flagship family of foundational models engineered specifically for Indian vernacular nuance and multi-modal audio pipelines.

Trained on high-fidelity localized datasets spanning Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Bengali, and Marathi, the models outperform mainstream global architectures on regional dialect translation benchmarks.

Co-founders Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar noted that democratizing open-source model weights is critical for Indian banks, healthcare providers, and regional governments to operate without data sovereignty risks.

title: India faces 53-60% talent gap in GenAI, cloud skills: TeamLease report
subtitle: Widening deficit between soaring corporate demand for LLM orchestration engineers and domestic engineering graduate readiness threatens deployment timelines.
summary: While Indian IT service firms sign multi-million dollar GenAI transformation contracts, acute shortages of senior prompt architects and RAG engineers challenge execution.
content: A comprehensive industry report released by TeamLease Digital indicates that domestic enterprise GCCs and system integrators face a 53% to 60% shortage of qualified GenAI engineers.
Despite producing over 1.5 million annual engineering graduates, fewer than 8% demonstrate proficiency with vector databases, embedding tokenization, and multi-agent frameworks like LangGraph.
Corporate training academies are pivoting to internal upskilling bootcamps and university partnerships to close the vacancy backlog of over 85,000 specialist positions.

title: Peak XV Partners leads $25M Series A round in Fabless Semiconductor startup NeuroEdge
subtitle: Custom sub-4nm processor architectures bring trillion-parameter neural network inference directly to smart edge sensors and industrial robotics.
summary: Fabless silicon innovator NeuroEdge secures growth equity to finance test tape-outs and sample silicon deliveries for autonomous vehicle cameras.
content: Deeptech fabless designer NeuroEdge has closed a $25 million Series A round spearheaded by Peak XV Partners with participation from Lightspeed India and prominent Silicon Valley angels.
The startup has engineered an ultra-low-power neural processing unit capable of running local transformer inference with 90% less thermal dissipation than standard x86 and GPU accelerators.
Commercial pilots are underway with global Tier-1 automotive manufacturers and aerospace drone developers.

title: Cynlr raises $10M to give industrial robotic arms human-like vision and tactile intuition
subtitle: Bengaluru deeptech company builds neuro-morphic visual intelligence that allows robotic manipulators to pick unoriented objects without CAD model pre-training.
summary: Robotics pioneer eliminates expensive custom mechanical fixtures by equipping multi-axis arms with real-time visual-spatial reasoning.
content: Industrial automation firm Cynlr has raised $10 million in fresh capital from institutional tech syndicates to scale its visual-cognition stack.

Traditional factory robots require rigid feeding lines where parts must arrive in mathematically predefined orientations. Cynlr's camera and neural perception engine mimic human stereoscopic hand-eye coordination.
The technology is already deployed across high-precision electronic assembly lines and automotive manufacturing hubs in Germany and Japan.

title: How Krutrim is scaling sovereign AI clusters with customized 10,000 GPU data centers
subtitle: Bhavish Aggarwal's AI venture rolls out cloud compute reservations for Indian startups, slashing API token costs by 40% compared to Western hyperscalers.
summary: India's first AI unicorn unveils end-to-end cloud platform featuring silicon acceleration, native Indic fine-tuning, and green solar-powered data centers.
content: Krutrim AI has begun provisioning enterprise access to its newly inaugurated hyperscale compute facility in Tamil Nadu, powered by over 10,000 high-performance AI accelerator chips.
The company positions its platform as a cost-efficient sovereign alternative to Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure for domestic generative AI startups.
Over 250 enterprise clients in fintech, logistics, and healthcare have transitioned baseline workloads to the Krutrim cloud stack.

title: From demo to deployment: Indian CIOs shift focus to RAG pipelines and on-prem inference
subtitle: Enterprise survey of 120 tech leaders reveals that 78% have moved past exploratory proof-of-concepts to productionize domain-specific AI workflows.
summary: Chief Information Officers prioritize retrieval-augmented generation to safeguard intellectual property while automating customer operations.
content: The initial phase of uncurated public chatbot experimentation has given way to disciplined corporate deployment across India's largest banking and telecommunications enterprises.
CIOs report that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) connected to internal knowledge bases provides hallucination-free output with clear audit trails.

title: Pharma's real AI challenge is embedding it into day-to-day operations: Karan Dhaudia
subtitle: Karan Dhaudia, Principal at Kearney, on how pharma companies are embedding AI into day-to-day operations, moving from pilots to building competitive moats, and the key challenges along the way.
summary: Karan Dhaudia, Principal at Kearney, on how pharma companies are embedding AI into day-to-day operations, moving from pilots to building competitive moats, and the key challenges along the way.
content: Artificial intelligence is no longer an experimental novelty in global biopharma. Over the past twenty-four months, nearly every top-50 life sciences multinational has launched exploratory generative AI and machine learning pilots spanning drug discovery, in-silico molecule docking, and automated medical regulatory writing.

Yet according to Karan Dhaudia, Principal at global management consulting firm Kearney, the genuine inflection point for pharmaceutical enterprises lies not in launching more pilots, but in integrating AI workflows deeply into the messy, governed reality of day-to-day operations.

“The primary bottleneck pharma companies face is organizational inertia compounded by strict GxP validation compliance,” Dhaudia explains. “When you operate in an industry where data lineage, clinical safety, and regulatory audits carry multi-million-dollar liabilities, you cannot simply deploy black-box foundation models. Embedding AI requires restructuring clinical trial recruitment pipelines, standardizing messy electronic lab notebooks, and upskilling scientific researchers.”

Dhaudia points out that the pharma organizations building durable competitive moats are focusing on three core operational pillars: sovereign clinical data architectures, outcome-based vendor accountability, and continuous model observability. Rather than chasing generic chatbot interfaces, leading teams are deploying specialized agentic workflows that compress patent review cycles from months to days while preserving airtight audit trails.

content: टेकस्पार्क्स का 15वां संस्करण इस साल 26 से 28 सितंबर के बीच बेंगलुरु के ताज वेस्ट एंड में आयोजित होने जा रहा है। इस साल की थीम है 'द न्यू टेक ऑर्डर' (The New Tech Order)। पिछले डेढ़ दशक से टेकस्पार्क्स भारत के टेक और स्टार्टअप इकोसिस्टम का सबसे बड़ा और विश्वसनीय मंच बना हुआ है, जिसने अनगिनत यूनिकॉर्न्स, इनोवेटर्स और नीति-निर्माताओं को एक साथ लाकर देश की डिजिटल विकास यात्रा को गति दी है।

इस साल का टेकस्पार्क्स भारत के टेक और इनोवेशन लैंडस्केप में आ रहे बड़े बदलावों को रेखांकित करेगा। आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस (AI), डीपटेक, फिनटेक, स्पेसटेक, सेमीकंडक्टर और क्वांटम कंप्यूटिंग जैसे उभरते क्षेत्रों में भारत की वैश्विक स्थिति पर गहन चर्चा होगी।

तीन दिवसीय इस महाकुंभ में 150 से अधिक अनुभवी वक्ता अपने विचार साझा करेंगे। इनमें केंद्रीय वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्री पीयूष गोयल, जेरोधा के नितिन कामथ, जोहो के श्रीधर वेम्बु, जोमैटो के दीपिंदर गोयल, और एडलवाइस म्यूचुअल फंड की राधिका गुप्ता शामिल हैं।

title: She couldn't do one pull-up. Today, Prableen Kaur Gill is Asia's No. 1 street lifter
subtitle: A former swimmer and pull-up coach, Prableen Kaur Gill shares her journey of grit, persistence, and breaking stereotypes in the male-dominated field of street lifting.
heroSubheading: Today, Prableen Kaur Gill is Asia’s No. 1 Street Lifter
author: Rekha Balakrishnan

milestones.title: The Humble Beginning (2020)
milestones.description: Walked into a calisthenics park unable to do a single pull-up. Qualified 2nd in her first contest 6 months later.

milestones.title: Historic National Record
milestones.description: Completed a weighted muscle-up with +13.75 kg plate load — the highest ever in Indian history.

milestones.title: Reconstructive Surgery Comeback (2024)
milestones.description: Suffered severe ankle fracture; trained exclusively upper body in a leg cast to return 5 kg stronger.

milestones.title: Asia's No. 1 Crown & Community
milestones.description: Ranked No. 1 in Asia by WSLA; now mentors 140+ women athletes across India.

mottoText: Strength has no gender. You don't ask for permission on the bar; you just pull.
leadStoryText: hen Prableen Kaur Gill decided to take up calisthenics, a form of strength training, she couldn't complete a single pull-up. But she was determined to change that. Six months later, she entered a competition where participants had to complete 10 pull-ups. Not only did she meet the target, she stood second.
philosophyQuote: I never started this journey to prove men wrong. I started it to prove to myself that human bone, muscle, and discipline have no predefined ceiling.
section1Title: From swimming to figuring things out
featureCaption: Prableen Kaur Gill with her All-India Calisthenics Championship Gold Medal.
section1Lead: orn and raised in Jalandhar, Punjab, Prableen was a competitive national-level swimmer throughout her school years. She spent hours every morning in the pool, developing cardiovascular endurance and disciplined work ethic.
section1Body: However, after graduating college and moving to Mumbai and later Hyderabad for work, sports took a backseat. The long desk hours and corporate pressure began to take a toll on her health.
section1PullquoteText: “I was feeling lethargic, weak, and disconnected from my physical self. I wanted to feel strong again. When I walked into a calisthenics park in 2020, I saw men hanging from bars doing incredible movements. There wasn't a single woman in sight. That sparked something inside me.”
section2Lead: Street lifting is demanding. A single competition requires maximum one-rep attempts across all four disciplines: pull-up, bar dip, muscle-up, and back squat. It requires tendon conditioning, immense grip strength, and an ironclad central nervous system.
section2ModernQuote: When I started adding weight to my pull-ups, people told me lifting heavy would make me bulky or ruin my posture. All the classic myths. Instead, my bone density increased, back pain vanished, and my confidence soared.
section2Body: In 2022, she entered the national circuit, sweeping gold in her weight category. By 2024, she was competing on the Asian championship circuit across Singapore, Thailand, and Kazakhstan.
calloutTitle: Resilience in the face of injury
calloutText: In early 2024, a severe ankle injury during a training session required reconstructive surgery, sidelining her from all lower-body movements for four months. 'Being on crutches was tough mentally. But it forced me to double down on upper-body pulling strength. When I returned to competition, my weighted pull-up had actually increased by five kilograms.'
section3Title: From digital diary to fitness community
section3Body1: Prableen began sharing her raw training footage on Instagram — including the failed attempts, ripped calluses, and slow progression. What began as a personal digital training log quickly grew into a community of over 95,000 followers.
section3Body2: Today, she coaches dozens of women across India and abroad through customized strength and pull-up programming. Many of her clients are homemakers, corporate professionals, and young girls who had never held a pull-up bar before.
takeawayText: “Watching a 45-year-old woman achieve her first unassisted pull-up gives me more joy than winning a medal. When a woman discovers she is physically strong, it changes how she walks into a boardroom, how she speaks, and how she navigates the world.”
audioNarrationText: She couldn't do one pull-up. Today, Prableen Kaur Gill is Asia's number one street lifter. A former swimmer and pull-up coach, Prableen shares her journey of grit, persistence, and breaking stereotypes in the male-dominated field of street lifting. Reported by Rekha Balakrishnan for HerStory.

title: Khadi Reinvented: Four women turning heritage weave into global fashion
subtitle: From rural looms in Varanasi to runways in Milan, these founders are making indigenous handloom luxury wear.
heroTitleAccent: Heritage Weave to Milan & Paris Runways
author: Aparna Banerji

milestones.title: Revival of 200-Count Khadi (2021)
milestones.description: Re-engineered ultra-fine handspun cotton yarn that breathes like silk without any chemical processing.

milestones.title: The Milan Runway Debut (2023)
milestones.description: First Indian all-women artisan cooperative invited to present zero-carbon couture at Sustainable Fashion Week.

milestones.title: Direct Artisan Fair-Share Model
milestones.description: Guaranteed 4.5× standard market daily wages to 280+ rural women hand-spinners in Varanasi.

milestones.title: Global Export Footprint (2026)
milestones.description: Shipping indigenous luxury garments to 14 countries while preserving 100% manual pit-loom techniques.

mottoText: Khadi is not nostalgic cloth for yesterday; it is the most modern, climate-resilient fabric for tomorrow.
leadStoryText: hen Devika Sharma and her three co-founders set up their first shared pit loom in a village outside Varanasi, local middlemen mocked them. Handloom was dying, they said. Today, four years later, their zero-carbon handspun collections grace luxury boutiques in Milan, Tokyo, and New York, sustaining over 280 artisan households.
philosophyQuote: True luxury is knowing the woman who spun your thread was paid with dignity, equity, and artistic ownership.
section1Title: From forgotten village looms to international runways
featureCaption: Varanasi weavers blending natural plant-dyed yarn on heritage wooden pit-looms.
section1Lead: orn into weaver families, the founders grew up watching master craftsmen abandon ancestral looms to take up odd construction jobs in nearby cities. Handloom was seen as unviable in an era of cheap fast fashion and synthetic powerlooms.
section1Body: The breakthrough came when they paired heritage botanical dyeing techniques with contemporary Scandinavian silhouettes, marketing khadi not as cheap souvenir cloth, but as rare, artisanal bespoke luxury.
section1PullquoteText: “We told our weavers: do not compromise on quality to compete with polyester factories. Slow down. Spin the finest thread you can imagine. We will find customers across the world who appreciate the heartbeat in each millimeter.”
section2Title: Rewriting the economics of sustainable fashion
section2Lead: Traditional supply chains left women spinners with barely ₹120 for an eight-hour shift of backbreaking charkha work. By establishing a direct co-ownership structure, the cooperative eliminated five tiers of brokers and commission agents.
section2ModernQuote: Fashion has poisoned rivers and underpaid women for half a century. We proved that ethical handcrafted fashion can be commercially profitable and globally competitive.
section2Body: In 2024, the brand launched its flagship regenerative collection dyed using temple flower waste and marigold blossoms, saving over 40,000 liters of potable water per batch.
calloutText: Every garment shipped by the collective carries a physical QR-code passport tracing the exact farmer who cultivated the organic rain-fed desi cotton, the woman who spun the hank, and the weaver who crafted the textile.
section3Body1: Beyond fair wages, the cooperative created a village healthcare corpus and scholarship fund that currently sponsors college tuition for 140 daughters of weavers.
section3Body2: Young women who once felt pressured into early marriages are now training as master dyers and quality controllers, earning higher monthly incomes than their village panchayat heads.
takeawayText: “When a rural woman becomes the primary breadwinner through her creative artistry, the social hierarchy of the entire village quietly transforms forever.”
audioNarrationText: Khadi Reinvented: Four women turning heritage weave into global fashion. From rural looms in Varanasi to runways in Milan, these founders are making indigenous handloom luxury wear. Reported by Aparna Banerji for HerStory.

title: How this 19-year-old researcher took algorithmic bias to Parliament
subtitle: Aditi Bhatt uncovered gender disparity in school admissions software and presented recommendations to lawmakers.

author: Priya Kale

milestones.title: The Algorithm Audit (2022)
milestones.description: Reverse-engineered automated school admission software, revealing an uncalibrated 22% penalty against female applicants.

milestones.title: Open-Source Fairness Framework
milestones.description: Built a lightweight Python bias detection library adopted by 40+ educational institutions nationwide.

milestones.description: Presented statistical proof and algorithmic accountability benchmarks directly to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on IT.

milestones.title: Youth AI Lab Initiative

mottoText: Code is never neutral. It inherits the prejudices of its creators unless we actively audit it for fairness.
leadStoryText: hen 19-year-old computer science sophomore Aditi Bhatt noticed peculiar score variances in an automated admissions portal used by leading technical institutions, she spent three sleepless weeks reverse-engineering the predictive neural network. What she found shocked the education department: historical bias was quietly baked into the screening code.
philosophyQuote: When algorithms automate decisions about our futures, questioning the code is not rebellion — it is fundamental democratic duty.
section1Title: From a dormitory desk audit to national policy
featureCaption: Aditi Bhatt demonstrating algorithmic testing models at the National AI Policy Summit.
section1Lead: diti grew up in Dehradun, coding on a refurbished laptop with an unsteady broadband connection. She developed a keen instinct for statistical anomalies while building machine learning models for high school science fairs.
section1Body: Her 84-page investigative audit proved that applicant scoring algorithms penalized candidates with career breaks or non-traditional extracurricular profiles — demographic patterns disproportionately common among female students.
section1PullquoteText: “I presented our code analysis to the vendor first. They said it was proprietary secret sauce. That’s when I realized: you cannot hide behind proprietary secrecy when human destinies are being decided.”
section2Title: Demystifying the black box of predictive software
section2Lead: Rather than seeking commercial patents, Aditi made the auditing suite freely accessible on GitHub. Within months, university student unions and independent data researchers verified her findings across four other public sector portals.
section2ModernQuote: If young women are not in the room writing and evaluating neural networks, the future of artificial intelligence will merely replicate the inequalities of the past.
section2Body: Her rigorous technical evidence prompted parliamentary lawmakers to propose mandatory third-party fairness audits for all automated decision-making platforms deployed in public services.
calloutText: Aditi's recommendations led to the introduction of statutory explainability mandates, requiring educational platforms to provide plain-language reasoning whenever an automated system rejects a student application.
section3Body1: Through her Youth AI Lab, Aditi conducts free weekend data clinics for undergraduate women, teaching reverse engineering, adversarial testing, and statistical ethics.
section3Body2: Over 600 students from tier-2 and tier-3 colleges have participated, publishing twenty-two peer-reviewed papers on bias remediation across regional languages.
takeawayText: “Never assume because a machine calculated a result that the result is just. Mathematics is innocent; the objective functions we program are deeply human.”
audioNarrationText: How this 19-year-old researcher took algorithmic bias to Parliament. Aditi Bhatt uncovered gender disparity in school admissions software and presented recommendations to lawmakers. Reported by Priya Kale for HerStory.

title: Women farmers of Vidarbha turning dryland tracts into organic profit
subtitle: Overcoming droughts and debt through millet cultivation and farmer collective bargaining.

author: Sunita Sharma

milestones.description: Rescued 18 forgotten drought-resistant millet varieties requiring 70% less water than cash crops.

milestones.title: Debt-Free Farm Transition
milestones.description: Shifted 650 acres of arid land from toxic pesticides to certified organic multi-tier polyculture.

milestones.title: Collective Direct Market Linkages
milestones.description: Bypassed exploitative middlemen, boosting member households net farm income by 310%.

mottoText: The soil does not belong to chemical giants. When women hold the seeds, the earth learns to blossom again.
leadStoryText: n the rain-shadow belt of Vidarbha, where erratic monsoons and predatory moneylenders once drove farm households into despair, Sunita Sharma and her neighbors decided to stop planting water-guzzling hybrid cotton. They turned back to the ancient grains of their grandmothers: drought-hardy, nutrient-rich millets that thrive in parched red earth.
philosophyQuote: Millets are not poor people's food. They are climate armor, economic freedom, and medicine for our mothers and children.
section1Title: Reviving forgotten grains in barren soil
featureCaption: Women farmers harvesting organic pearl millet (Bajra) in Vidarbha fields.
section1Lead: our consecutive drought seasons had devastated the region by 2019. High fertilizer costs and mounting debt had left dozens of families contemplating abandoning farming altogether.
section1Body: Sunita traveled on foot across tribal hamlets to collect heirloom finger millet (Ragi), foxtail millet, and kodo seeds that had survived centuries without artificial chemicals or groundwater depletion.
section1PullquoteText: “The agricultural extension officers told us millets had no market value. We told them: if the climate is changing, the city will soon hunger for what survives without rain. We were right.”
section2Title: Breaking the vicious cycle of chemical debt
section2Lead: By switching from single-crop chemical farming to five-layer organic companion planting, the women slashed input costs by 85%. Companion pulses naturally fixed nitrogen into the depleted topsoil.
section2ModernQuote: We stopped buying expensive synthetic inputs in plastic bags. Our cows, compost heaps, and neem extracts gave the earth everything it needed to heal.
section2Body: In 2023, the collective established their own solar-powered grain de-husking and flour mill, packaging stone-ground organic millet flours for direct sale to organic supermarkets in Mumbai and Pune.
calloutText: The farmers pooled surplus grain into a community emergency grain bank. During unexpected weather shocks, member families borrow grain with zero interest, completely eliminating visits to predatory village moneylenders.
section3Title: From subsistence farming to retail sovereignty
section3Body1: Today, the collective’s brand generates over ₹3.8 Crore in annual revenue, with all profits redistributed to women landholders in proportion to their harvested acreage.
section3Body2: Bank loans that had haunted families for three generations have been settled in full. For the first time, daughters from these farm families are attending agricultural universities.
takeawayText: “When women own the seed bank and the bank account, drought ceases to be a death sentence and becomes an invitation to innovate.”
audioNarrationText: Women farmers of Vidarbha turning dryland tracts into organic profit. Overcoming droughts and debt through millet cultivation and farmer collective bargaining. Reported by Sunita Sharma for HerStory.

mottoText: When a village woman hears her own dialect talking about constitutional rights on audio, fear turns into collective power.
leadStoryText: very Tuesday evening under the banyan tree of a remote village in Chhindwara, women gather not around a television, but around a simple portable speaker connected to a basic keypad phone. The voice on the audio belongs to Parvati, a local mother of three, speaking in Gondi about property inheritances and neonatal nutrition.
philosophyQuote: Audio transcends literacy barriers. Your voice is your vote, your power, and your unvarnished truth.
section1Title: Broadcasting across literacy and language barriers
featureCaption: Community reporter conducting field interviews with tribal elder women.
section1Lead: ith literacy rates among tribal women in central India lagging behind national averages, printed newspapers and digital text portals failed to reach the women who needed legal and medical information the most.
section1Body: Nandita Sengupta designed an interactive voice response platform where any woman with a ₹900 feature phone could dial a missed call and receive an automated callback delivering 4-minute hyper-local audio dispatches.
section1PullquoteText: “We didn't want fancy podcasts for urban elites with noise-canceling headphones. We wanted raw, authentic audio in the mother tongue of the woman sitting by the kitchen hearth.”
section2Title: Investigative audio dispatches that force action
section2Lead: The community newsroom soon expanded beyond educational drama into hard-hitting local investigative reporting, documenting broken water pumps, absenteeism at public health centers, and illegal wage cuts.
section2ModernQuote: Local district officials used to ignore written petitions from poor women. But when an audio recording of a village mother plays on a speaker in the collector’s office, issues get fixed within 48 hours.
section2Body: In over 180 recorded instances, audio broadcasts have directly triggered prompt administrative repairs of drinking water borewells and delivery of delayed social welfare pensions.
calloutTitle: A confidential helpline for domestic welfare
calloutText: The audio platform includes a secure voice mailbox where women can anonymously leave voice notes detailing domestic harassment or community grievances, connecting them directly with legal aid volunteers.
section3Title: The expanding footprint of community newsrooms
section3Body1: From a single pilot district, Gaon Vani now produces original programming in 18 tribal and regional dialects across Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha.
section3Body2: Over 120 rural women now draw regular professional monthly stipends as certified community journalists and podcast producers.
takeawayText: “Freedom of expression is hollow if people who cannot read or write are silenced. Oral journalism returns media to its most ancient, democratic root.”

milestones.description: Successfully located and extracted 38 stranded mountaineers during sudden blizzard whiteouts.

mottoText: The mountains do not care about your ego. Up here, survival belongs to those who listen, prepare, and stay humble.
leadStoryText: t 14,200 feet on the wind-battered slopes of the Pin Parvati Pass, temperatures plunge to minus twenty degrees within minutes of sunset. While commercial trekking companies retreat to basecamp, Rashi Goel and her pack of four trained indigenous Gaddi shepherd hounds strap on thermal harnesses to begin their nightly reconnaissance.
philosophyQuote: Courage in the mountains is not defying gravity; it is keeping your head calm when the whiteout takes every horizon away.
section1Title: Pioneering canine mountain rescue in India
featureCaption: Rashi Goel training alpine search hounds in deep snowpack near Spiti.
section1Lead: hile European Alps boast professional avalanche search teams, Himalayan trekking corridors have historically relied on delayed manual military helicopter sorties that can take days during adverse weather.
section1Body: Rashi recognized that the indigenous Himalayan Gaddi sheepdog possessed unrivaled thermal insulation, lung capacity, and olfactory perception in thin oxygen atmospheres.
section1PullquoteText: “People spent lakhs importing Saint Bernards that struggled to breathe in our rocky scree. The local mountain dogs had evolved for thousands of years right here. They knew every scent of the snow.”
section2Title: Minutes make the difference under snow
section2Lead: An avalanche victim’s survival probability plummets drastically after the first fifteen minutes of burial. Rashi’s canine units can scent a buried human through six feet of compact ice in under four minutes.
section2ModernQuote: When my dog Bheema begins frantically digging into an icy snowdrift, you don’t question him. You start shoveling with everything you have.
section2Body: In November 2024, her team extracted an entire four-person international research team caught in an unseasonal blizzard, earning national recognition from the Ministry of Civil Aviation.
calloutText: Rashi has trained 24 young women from Spiti and Kinnaur as certified high-altitude wilderness first responders, dismantling the long-held taboo that only male porters could lead extreme mountain expeditions.
section3Body1: In parallel with rescue work, the team runs clean-up expeditions along the high passes, ensuring waste left by unchecked adventure tourism is packed down to recycling centers.
section3Body2: Her foundation now provides free veterinary care and winter shelters for over 200 working shepherd dogs across upper Himachal Pradesh.
takeawayText: “The mountain is our temple. If we learn to walk with its animals and respect its fury, it teaches us an inner stillness no city can give.”
audioNarrationText: Himalayan Shepherds: High-altitude rescue mission with mountain hounds. At 14,000 feet, Rashi Goel and her pack of trained mountain dogs guide trekkers through treacherous passes. Reported by Rashi Goel for HerStory.

title: How a mobile bicycle library is educating 5,000 rural girls in Bihar

mottoText: A book placed in the hands of a rural girl does not merely teach her letters; it shows her that the world is bigger than her courtyard.
leadStoryText: cross the unpaved mud embankments of Sitamarhi district, the faint sound of a bicycle bell at 4 PM brings dozens of schoolgirls running with canvas bags. Mounted on the rear rack of each bicycle is a custom-welded wooden crate stocked with colorful illustrated astronomy books, biographies of women scientists, and regional storybooks.
philosophyQuote: If children in remote villages cannot walk kilometers to reach a library, then the library must pedal directly to their doorsteps.
section1Title: Breaking through the barrier of distance
featureCaption: Village girls gathering for an open-air weekend reading circle under a banyan tree.
section1Lead: hen state schools shut down during the pandemic, girls in agricultural households bore the heaviest burden of domestic chores, often permanently losing their reading fluency within months.
section1Body: Vandana Shukla, a former schoolteacher, refused to let two decades of progress in female literacy disappear. She strapped forty books to her father’s old bicycle and began riding from village to village.
section1PullquoteText: “Parents told me: why give her books when she has to cook and graze goats? I told them: let her read for just thirty minutes after sunset. If she doesn’t become more alert and responsible, I will stop coming. None of them ever asked me to stop.”
section2Title: Creating a network of bicycle librarians
section2Lead: Within two years, older girls who had excelled in the reading circles volunteered to become librarians themselves. Today, a fleet of 60 pedal-powered mobile libraries crisscrosses sixty-two villages daily.
section2ModernQuote: Carrying thirty books on a bicycle through monsoon mud is tiring. But when you see an eight-year-old girl finish reading her first book about Kalpana Chawla, all fatigue disappears.
section2Body: In addition to literature, the libraries carry hands-on solar microscope kits and basic arithmetic puzzles that make science tactile and fun.
calloutText: The project runs remedial scholarship camps where volunteer college students coach girls for national matriculation exams, resulting in a 94% pass rate among participating students.
section3Body1: Mothers who were illiterate are now attending evening literacy sessions alongside their daughters, learning to sign bank documents and read crop purchase receipts.
section3Body2: Over four hundred young girls who had dropped out of school have returned to formal education, with several entering nursing and polytechnic institutes.
takeawayText: “When you educate a girl in a village, you do not just change one life; you break an ancestral cycle of silence and poverty for generations to come.”

milestones.description: Established a village-level maintenance fund generating sustainable technical incomes for certified women engineers.

mottoText: You do not need a university engineering degree to harness sunlight. Wisdom, patience, and community ownership are enough.
leadStoryText: n the dunes of the Thar desert, night historically meant complete darkness broken only by the flickering, choking black smoke of kerosene wick lamps. Today, forty remote hamlets glow with clean, warm electric light generated by rooftop solar microgrids engineered, soldered, and maintained exclusively by local tribal women.
philosophyQuote: Energy independence is the cornerstone of dignity. When village women govern the power grid, development works for everyone.
featureCaption: Solar technicians assembling battery storage units in their community workshop.
section1Lead: any of the women in the Surya Sakhi collective had never attended formal school and could not read printed circuit schematics.
section1Body: By developing color-coded diagrams, tactile soldering jigs, and practical mnemonic songs, the program trained rural grandmothers into skilled photovoltaic technicians capable of troubleshooting battery charge controllers.
section1PullquoteText: “When the men in the village saw grandmothers climbing onto roofs with solar panels and wrenches, they laughed. But when darkness fell and our bulbs switched on while the government lines were broken, everyone fell silent.”
section2Title: Eliminating kerosene soot and lung disease
section2Lead: Inhaling kerosene lamp fumes for four hours every evening is equivalent to smoking two packs of cigarettes. Replacing these lamps with clean LED solar lanterns caused an immediate drop in childhood respiratory illnesses.
section2ModernQuote: Our children used to cough all night and struggle to study by dim flames. Now, they finish their homework under bright solar lights without burning their eyes.
section2Body: The microgrids also power community cold storage units for medicines and mobile phone charging kiosks that save villagers twenty-kilometer trips to town.
calloutText: Each household contributes ₹60 per month — half of what they previously spent on kerosene — into a communal repair fund that pays the women technicians regular maintenance salaries and covers battery replacements.
section3Title: Scaling clean energy across tribal belts
section3Body1: The Solar Sisters model has gained international accolades, inspiring similar decentralized community microgrids in tribal areas across Jharkhand and Odisha.
section3Body2: Over 140 women technicians have been certified, transforming once-marginalized tribal women into celebrated leaders of the green energy transition.
takeawayText: “True renewable energy is not just about silicon and solar cells; it is about putting the power directly into the hands of the people who need it most.”
audioNarrationText: Solar Sisters: Electrifying 40 off-grid tribal hamlets in Rajasthan. Barefoot solar engineers assembling clean microgrids and empowering rural women technicians. Reported by Geeta Nair for HerStory.

milestones.title: Direct Sourcing from 450 Tribal Foragers
milestones.description: Procured forest herbs and cold-pressed botanical oils directly from indigenous women foragers in Uttarakhand.

mottoText: Do not dilute your vision for quick venture money. A profitable business built on customer trust can outlast any hype cycle.
leadStoryText: hen 34-year-old Rekha Sharma took ₹500 from her monthly vegetable budget in 2019 to buy cold-pressed mustard oil, beeswax, and raw turmeric, she was desperate to heal her daughter’s persistent eczema after commercial creams failed. Today, that kitchen experiment has grown into a ₹12 Crore certified organic wellness powerhouse without taking a single rupee of venture capital.
philosophyQuote: Profitability is the truest freedom. When your customers fund your growth, you never have to ask permission to do what is right.
section1Title: From hand-poured glass jars to retail distribution
featureCaption: Rekha inspecting botanical distillation batches at her Jaipur research laboratory.
section1Lead: n an era where direct-to-consumer beauty brands raised hundreds of crores of venture funding to burn on digital advertising, Rekha took the old-fashioned path: word-of-mouth efficacy and uncompromising ingredient purity.
section1Body: She personally hand-delivered her first hundred glass jars to mothers in her neighborhood, asking for honest reviews and refining the formulations until results spoke for themselves.
section1PullquoteText: “Investors told me: water down the formulas, use synthetic preservatives, and spend your money acquiring customers online. I told them: I would rather sell to ten customers who buy for life than thousand customers who never return.”
section2Title: Ethical sourcing that sustains mountain foragers
section2Lead: Rather than buying bulk extracts from commercial chemical distributors, VedaRoots established direct fair-trade sourcing partnerships with women herb gatherers across high-altitude Himalayan valleys.
section2ModernQuote: Every bottle of face oil we ship directly supports the livelihood of mountain women who know the rhythm of when wild herbs should be harvested without damaging the forest.
section2Body: In 2024, the brand attained European COSMOS organic certification, opening direct export avenues to Germany, Switzerland, and the United Arab Emirates.
calloutText: While competitors spent 60% of revenue on social media influencers and ran deep net losses, VedaRoots has generated consecutive net profit margins above 26% year-on-year for five straight fiscal years.
section3Body1: Her modern formulation facility in Jaipur employs over 70 women, providing free childcare and healthcare benefits for all factory associates.
section3Body2: Rekha hosts free monthly incubation workshops for aspiring women founders, helping them navigate food and drug licensing, packaging compliance, and financial accounting.
takeawayText: “You do not need an MBA or an investor syndicate to build a great company. Start in your kitchen, solve a real human pain, and never compromise your standards.”
audioNarrationText: Bootstrapping ₹12 Cr organic skincare from a single kitchen stove. How Rekha Sharma turned a ₹500 grocery investment into an 800-store distribution powerhouse. Reported by Rekha Balakrishnan for HerStory.

title: Four Indian brands putting a new spin on khadi
excerpt: From contemporary cuts and silhouettes to reimagining the loom itself, these brands are proving that India's handspun heritage fabric is more relevant than ever.
summary: From contemporary cuts and silhouettes to reimagining the loom itself, these brands are proving that India's handspun heritage fabric is more relevant than ever.
content: Khadi is no longer confined to traditional national occasions. A rising wave of contemporary homegrown brands is fusing handspun, zero-carbon cotton and silk with modern cuts, neutral tones, and durable tailoring.

By collaborating directly with weaver clusters across West Bengal, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh, these labels ensure living wages for rural artisans while introducing khadi to Gen Z and millennial wardrobes.

“We want people to touch the fabric and realise that it is the ultimate natural luxury: breathable in heat, insulated in cool evenings, and entirely biodegradable,” says one of the featured designers.
